hints.title: Multi-List Coverage Window
hints.text: A valid range must contain at least one element from each of the k sorted input lists.

hints.title: Min-Heap Pointers and Maximum Tracker
hints.text: Insert the first element of each list into a min-priority queue and track the current maximum element in the window.

hints.title: Advancing Minimum List Pointer
hints.text: Pop min element from heap. Update best range with [min_val, max_val] if window is narrower. Advance pointer in the list containing min_val, update max_val, and push next element into heap. Terminate when any list is exhausted.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
import heapq
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def smallestRange(self, nums: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        heap = []
        curr_max = float("-inf")
        for i in range(len(nums)):
            heapq.heappush(heap, (nums[i][0], i, 0))
            curr_max = max(curr_max, nums[i][0])

        best_range = [float("-inf"), float("inf")]

        while heap:
            val, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if curr_max - val < best_range[1] - best_range[0]:
                best_range = [val, curr_max]
            if c + 1 == len(nums[r]):
                break
            nxt_val = nums[r][c + 1]
            curr_max = max(curr_max, nxt_val)
            heapq.heappush(heap, (nxt_val, r, c + 1))

        return best_range
```

variables: N: total number of elements across all lists
complexity.notes: Min-heap maintains active window across all K lists.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all possible pair bounds requires combinatorial checks.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Min-heap of size K guarantees optimal window span maintenance in logarithmic time.
